subject.title: fix(acpx): drain leased descendants when turns are aborted

question: Should ACPX cancellation always close and evict the live runtime handle, and should unverifiable or undrainable stale ACPX leases prevent backend registration?
rationale: These are deliberate compatibility and availability policy changes that tests and process proof cannot authorize on behalf of ACPX/control-plane owners.

options.title: Accept fail-closed containment
options.body: Close and evict the handle on cancellation and refuse ACPX registration until stale owned processes are verifiably drained.

options.title: Add compatibility and recovery mode
options.body: Preserve current defaults while offering strict containment and an operator-visible stale-lease recovery workflow.

options.title: Retain cooperative cancellation
options.body: Keep reusable handles and non-blocking startup, accepting that protocol cancellation alone cannot prove detached process containment.

recommendation.title: Accept fail-closed containment
recommendation.body: Close and evict the handle on cancellation and refuse ACPX registration until stale owned processes are verifiably drained.

likelyOwner.reason: Current-main history makes this the strongest available owner signal for the ACPX lifecycle contract.
